/-!
# Erdős–Oler conjecture

Packing $n$ unit circles in an equilateral triangle asks for the smallest side length of an
equilateral triangle that contains $n$ unit circles with pairwise disjoint interiors.
The Erdős–Oler conjecture states that if $n$ is a triangular number, then the smallest such
side length for $n - 1$ circles is the same as for $n$ circles.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Circle packing in an equilateral triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle_packing_in_an_equilateral_triangle)
- Oler, Norman (1961), ["A finite packing problem"](https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1961-018-7),
  Canadian Mathematical Bulletin, 4 (2): 153–155
- Melissen, Hans (1993),
  ["Densest packings of congruent circles in an equilateral triangle"](https://doi.org/10.2307/2324212),
  The American Mathematical Monthly, 100 (10): 916–925
-/

blocks.docstring:
The closed equilateral triangle of side length `s` with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(s, 0)$ and
$(s / 2, s \sqrt{3} / 2)$.

The side length is a nonnegative real, so that `equilateralTriangle s` is always the equilateral
triangle of side length $s$. Every equilateral triangle of side length $s$ in the plane is
congruent to this one, so fixing it loses no generality when packing circles into it.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Affine.Simplex.Equilateral / Affine.Triangle (Mathlib), SquarePacking.Square (repo); convexHull ℝ of explicit points was used instead.
justification.name: ErdosOlerConjecture.equilateralTriangle
justification.why_needed: The closed equilateral triangle of side length s (s : ℝ≥0), as the convex hull of the vertices (0,0), (s,0), (s/2, s√3/2) in ℝ². Mathlib has Affine.Simplex.Equilateral but no ready-made 'the equilateral triangle of side s as a subset of the plane'. Fixing one triangle is WLOG since all equilateral triangles of side s are congruent and the circles may be placed anywhere. Using ℝ≥0 prevents negative s from producing a reflected triangle of side |s| (which would destroy the least element). A proved test lemma checks that the three vertices are pairwise at distance s.

blocks.text:
/--
The closed equilateral triangle of side length `s` with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(s, 0)$ and
$(s / 2, s \sqrt{3} / 2)$.

The side length is a nonnegative real, so that `equilateralTriangle s` is always the equilateral
triangle of side length $s$. Every equilateral triangle of side length $s$ in the plane is
congruent to this one, so fixing it loses no generality when packing circles into it.
-/
noncomputable def equilateralTriangle (s : ℝ≥0) : Set ℝ² :=
  convexHull ℝ {!₂[0, 0], !₂[(s : ℝ), 0], !₂[(s : ℝ) / 2, s * √3 / 2]}

blocks.docstring:
The set of side lengths `s` such that `n` unit circles can be packed in the equilateral triangle
of side length `s`: there are `n` centres such that each closed unit disc lies in the triangle,
and the open unit discs are pairwise disjoint (so the circles may touch but not overlap).

justification.closest_existing_considered: SquarePacking.Packing (FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/SquarePacking.lean), which packs isometric images of a base shape via ℝ² ≃ᵢ ℝ²; for circles a centre-based description is equivalent and simpler, and importing another problem file was avoided.
justification.name: ErdosOlerConjecture.packableSides
justification.why_needed: The set of side lengths s : ℝ≥0 such that n unit circles can be packed in equilateralTriangle s: there exist centres c : Fin n → ℝ² with each closed unit disc Metric.closedBall (c i) 1 inside the triangle and the open discs Metric.ball (c i) 1 pairwise disjoint (circles may touch, not overlap). This is the standard notion of a circle packing; the least element of this set is the optimal side length. A test lemma records that packableSides 0 = Set.univ, explaining why k ≥ 2 is needed.

blocks.name: packableSides
blocks.text:
/--
The set of side lengths `s` such that `n` unit circles can be packed in the equilateral triangle
of side length `s`: there are `n` centres such that each closed unit disc lies in the triangle,
and the open unit discs are pairwise disjoint (so the circles may touch but not overlap).
-/
def packableSides (n : ℕ) : Set ℝ≥0 :=
  {s | ∃ c : Fin n → ℝ², (∀ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) 1 ⊆ equilateralTriangle s) ∧
    Pairwise fun i j ↦ Disjoint (Metric.ball (c i) 1) (Metric.ball (c j) 1)}

@[category test, AMS 51]
theorem dist_vertices (s : ℝ≥0) :
    dist (!₂[0, 0] : ℝ²) !₂[(s : ℝ), 0] = s ∧
      dist (!₂[0, 0] : ℝ²) !₂[(s : ℝ) / 2, s * √3 / 2] = s ∧
      dist (!₂[(s : ℝ), 0] : ℝ²) !₂[(s : ℝ) / 2, s * √3 / 2] = s := by
  have h3 : (√3 : ℝ) ^ 2 = 3 := Real.sq_sqrt (by norm_num)
  simp only [EuclideanSpace.dist_eq, Fin.sum_univ_two, Matrix.cons_val_zero,
    Matrix.cons_val_one, Matrix.cons_val_fin_one, Real.dist_eq, sq_abs]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  all_goals rw [Real.sqrt_eq_iff_eq_sq (by positivity) s.coe_nonneg]; ring_nf
  all_goals try (rw [h3]; ring)

@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_oler_conjecture (n k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hn : n = k * (k + 1) / 2) :
    ∃ s, IsLeast (packableSides (n - 1)) s ∧ IsLeast (packableSides n) s := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**The Erdős–Oler conjecture.**
If $n$ is a triangular number, then packing $n - 1$ unit circles in an equilateral triangle
requires a triangle of the same size as packing $n$ unit circles: the least side length of an
equilateral triangle in which $n - 1$ unit circles can be packed equals the least side length
of an equilateral triangle in which $n$ unit circles can be packed. Formally, there is one side
length `s` that is the least element of both sets of admissible side lengths.

Here $n = k(k + 1) / 2$ with $k \ge 2$: for $k = 1$ (that is, $n = 1$) the statement would
compare packing one circle with packing no circles at all, which is degenerate.

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified Prop: for every triangular number n = k(k+1)/2 (k ≥ 2 needed, since n = 1 vs. 0 circles is degenerate), the least side length of an equilateral triangle admitting a packing of n−1 unit circles equals that for n unit circles; 'size' means side length (equivalently, the same optimal triangle), the optimum should be phrased as an infimum/IsLeast over side lengths with care about open vs. closed discs (cf. Packing in Wikipedia/SquarePacking.lean), and the article's 'remove one circle from the hexagonal packing' gloss and the 'true for n ≤ 15' remark are not separate questions.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the slot faithfully in substance (closed unit discs in a closed equilateral triangle with disjoint interiors, or the equivalent open-disc/open-triangle convention; triangular numbers n = k(k+1)/2 with k ≥ 2; equality of least side lengths). c01 was chosen because it follows the SquarePacking.lean idiom (IsLeast over the set of admissible side lengths, as the decomposition notes suggest), uses nonnegative side lengths so no junk values or sign issues arise, avoids reliance on sInf's default on ∅/unbounded sets, and includes a proven test that the model triangle has pairwise vertex distances exactly s plus a boundary-case test for zero circles. Edits: removed the unneeded `open Real`, and added one sentence to the theorem docstring making explicit that the ∃ s, IsLeast ∧ IsLeast form asserts a common least side length.

context:
Circle packing in an equilateral triangle is a packing problem in discrete mathematics where the objective is to pack n unit circles into the smallest possible equilateral triangle.  Optimal solutions have been proved for n ≤ 15, and for any triangular number of circles, and conjectures are available for n ≤ 34.
A conjecture of Paul Erdős and Norman Oler states that, if n is a triangular number, then the optimal packings of n − 1 and of n circles have the same side length: that is, according to the conjecture, an optimal packing for n − 1 circles can be found by removing any single circle from the optimal hexagonal packing of n circles. This conjecture is now known to be true for n ≤ 15. In a paper by Graham and Lubachevsky concerning solutions for 22 ≤ n ≤ 34 they also conjectured seven infinite families of optimal solutions in addition to the one by Erdős and Oler. These families give conjectured solutions for many more numbers, including n = 37, 40, 42, 43, 46, 49.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős–Oler conjecture

Packing $n$ unit circles in an equilateral triangle asks for the smallest side length of an
equilateral triangle that contains $n$ unit circles with pairwise disjoint interiors.
The Erdős–Oler conjecture states that if $n$ is a triangular number, then the smallest such
side length for $n - 1$ circles is the same as for $n$ circles.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Circle packing in an equilateral triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle_packing_in_an_equilateral_triangle)
- Oler, Norman (1961), ["A finite packing problem"](https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1961-018-7),
  Canadian Mathematical Bulletin, 4 (2): 153–155
- Melissen, Hans (1993),
  ["Densest packings of congruent circles in an equilateral triangle"](https://doi.org/10.2307/2324212),
  The American Mathematical Monthly, 100 (10): 916–925
-/

open EuclideanGeometry

open scoped NNReal

namespace ErdosOlerConjecture

/--
The closed equilateral triangle of side length `s` with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(s, 0)$ and
$(s / 2, s \sqrt{3} / 2)$.

The side length is a nonnegative real, so that `equilateralTriangle s` is always the equilateral
triangle of side length $s$. Every equilateral triangle of side length $s$ in the plane is
congruent to this one, so fixing it loses no generality when packing circles into it.
-/
noncomputable def equilateralTriangle (s : ℝ≥0) : Set ℝ² :=
  convexHull ℝ {!₂[0, 0], !₂[(s : ℝ), 0], !₂[(s : ℝ) / 2, s * √3 / 2]}

/--
The set of side lengths `s` such that `n` unit circles can be packed in the equilateral triangle
of side length `s`: there are `n` centres such that each closed unit disc lies in the triangle,
and the open unit discs are pairwise disjoint (so the circles may touch but not overlap).
-/
def packableSides (n : ℕ) : Set ℝ≥0 :=
  {s | ∃ c : Fin n → ℝ², (∀ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) 1 ⊆ equilateralTriangle s) ∧
    Pairwise fun i j ↦ Disjoint (Metric.ball (c i) 1) (Metric.ball (c j) 1)}

/-- The three vertices of `equilateralTriangle s` are pairwise at distance `s`. -/
@[category test, AMS 51]
theorem dist_vertices (s : ℝ≥0) :
    dist (!₂[0, 0] : ℝ²) !₂[(s : ℝ), 0] = s ∧
      dist (!₂[0, 0] : ℝ²) !₂[(s : ℝ) / 2, s * √3 / 2] = s ∧
      dist (!₂[(s : ℝ), 0] : ℝ²) !₂[(s : ℝ) / 2, s * √3 / 2] = s := by
  have h3 : (√3 : ℝ) ^ 2 = 3 := Real.sq_sqrt (by norm_num)
  simp only [EuclideanSpace.dist_eq, Fin.sum_univ_two, Matrix.cons_val_zero,
    Matrix.cons_val_one, Matrix.cons_val_fin_one, Real.dist_eq, sq_abs]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  all_goals rw [Real.sqrt_eq_iff_eq_sq (by positivity) s.coe_nonneg]; ring_nf
  all_goals try (rw [h3]; ring)

/-- Zero circles can be packed in an equilateral triangle of any side length. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem packableSides_zero : packableSides 0 = Set.univ := by
  ext s
  simp [packableSides]

/--
**The Erdős–Oler conjecture.**
If $n$ is a triangular number, then packing $n - 1$ unit circles in an equilateral triangle
requires a triangle of the same size as packing $n$ unit circles: the least side length of an
equilateral triangle in which $n - 1$ unit circles can be packed equals the least side length
of an equilateral triangle in which $n$ unit circles can be packed. Formally, there is one side
length `s` that is the least element of both sets of admissible side lengths.

Here $n = k(k + 1) / 2$ with $k \ge 2$: for $k = 1$ (that is, $n = 1$) the statement would
compare packing one circle with packing no circles at all, which is degenerate.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_oler_conjecture (n k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hn : n = k * (k + 1) / 2) :
    ∃ s, IsLeast (packableSides (n - 1)) s ∧ IsLeast (packableSides n) s := by
  sorry

end ErdosOlerConjecture

items: 'Size' is taken to mean side length (as in the article: 'the optimal packings of n − 1 and of n circles have the same side length'); the optimum is phrased with IsLeast on the set of feasible side lengths, following the SquarePacking.lean idiom.

The statement is ∃ s, IsLeast (packableSides (n-1)) s ∧ IsLeast (packableSides n) s. This asserts that both least side lengths exist and coincide. Existence of the minimum is a true (compactness) fact under this model, since the constraints (closed discs in a closed triangle, open discs disjoint) are closed and feasibility is upward closed in s, so the feasible set is [s_n, ∞); the article also presupposes optimal packings exist. Alternatives considered: sInf equality (risks degenerate 0 = 0 conventions) or ∀ s, IsLeast ↔ IsLeast (vacuous if no minima).

Packing convention: each closed unit disc lies in the closed triangle and the open unit discs are pairwise disjoint, i.e. circles may touch each other and the triangle boundary but do not overlap. This is equivalent to the open-disc-in-open-triangle convention of SquarePacking.lean.
'Unit circles' are taken to be circles of radius 1 (consistent with the Wikipedia table, e.g. side 2√3 for n = 1); the conjecture is scale invariant anyway.

Triangular numbers are written n = k * (k + 1) / 2 in ℕ (exact division). k ≥ 2 (i.e. n ≥ 3) is required: for k = 1 one would compare packing one circle with packing zero circles, and packableSides 0 = Set.univ (its least element 0 is not in packableSides 1), so the formal statement would be false there for degenerate reasons; k = 0 gives n = 0 and n − 1 truncates.

A single fixed equilateral triangle with vertices (0,0), (s,0), (s/2, s√3/2) is used instead of quantifying over all equilateral triangles; this loses no generality because the circle centres are arbitrary and all equilateral triangles of side s are congruent.
The article's remarks ('remove one circle from the hexagonal packing', 'true for n ≤ 15', Graham–Lubachevsky families) are not formalized, per the decomposition notes.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities in the source: 'size' is read as side length (the Wikipedia article says 'the same side length'; any size measure is equivalent by similarity); 'unit circles' as discs of radius 1 (consistent with the article's table, and the conjecture is scale-invariant); the optimum is the least admissible side length. The formal statement asserts existence of a common minimum (∃ s, IsLeast A s ∧ IsLeast B s); the minima exist by a standard compactness/closedness argument, so this is equivalent to equality of the two optimal side lengths (equivalently of the sInf-based `minSideLength` used by c02/c04/c06/c07/c08, whose admissible sets are nonempty and bounded below). Fixing the triangle in a canonical position (c01–c05) is equivalent to quantifying over all equilateral triangles (c06–c08) by isometry invariance of the packing condition. k ≥ 2 excludes the degenerate n = 1 case (0 circles fit in any triangle, so the formal statement would be false there for trivial reasons) as the decomposition table requires. Rejected alternatives: c03 imports the SquarePacking problem file and reuses its local `Packing` (acceptable in the repo but heavier and tagged AMS 51 only); c05 lacks tests for its bespoke definitions; the sInf-based candidates are faithful but rely (correctly) on the unproved-in-file nonemptiness of the admissible sets. No candidate had an omission. The article's 'remove one circle from the hexagonal packing' gloss and the 'true for n ≤ 15' remark are not formalized, per the decomposition table.
